name: Vitamin B12 and/or folate deficiency
rawContent:
# Vitamin B12 and/or folate deficiency: Core Condition Reference

## Overview
Deficiency of vitamin B12 and/or folate causes impaired DNA synthesis leading to megaloblastic anaemia; B12 deficiency may also cause neurological dysfunction.

overview.definition: Deficiency of vitamin B12 and/or folate causes impaired DNA synthesis leading to megaloblastic anaemia; B12 deficiency may also cause neurological dysfunction.
overview.epidemiology: Common in malnutrition, malabsorption, pernicious anaemia, and certain medications.
overview.pathophysiology: Deficient cofactors impair erythropoiesis causing macrocytosis and ineffective haematopoiesis.

atypicalPresentations: Isolated neuropsychiatric symptoms with minimal anaemia

firstLine: Ferritin and haemolysis screen if mixed picture
secondLine: Intrinsic factor/parietal cell antibodies for pernicious anaemia

diagnosis.criteria: Biochemical deficiency with compatible blood count/clinical features and exclusion of alternative causes.

firstLine: Replace B12 promptly when deficient (especially if neurological signs)
Folate replacement once B12 status addressed
Treat underlying cause and counsel on diet/medications
secondLine: Transfusion only if severe symptomatic anaemia per senior plan

monitoring: Repeat FBC and symptom review; lifelong B12 replacement in pernicious anaemia

drugs.name: Hydroxocobalamin
drugs.dosing: Per local loading and maintenance schedule.
drugs.notes: Give B12 before isolated folate if both possible.

drugs.name: Folic acid
drugs.mechanism: Replaces folate needed for DNA synthesis.
drugs.dosing: Typically daily oral replacement per cause/severity.
drugs.notes: Do not treat isolated macrocytosis with folate alone if B12 deficiency not excluded.

content.prognosis: Haematological response is usually good with treatment; delayed B12 neuropathy may be incompletely reversible.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Recognize macrocytic patterns, start safe replacement strategy, and ensure follow-up for cause and response.
content.escalation: Escalate if severe anaemia, neurological deficits, pancytopenia, or diagnostic uncertainty.
content.keySafetyConsiderations: Never start folate alone when B12 deficiency is possible.
